text:
tom: Heads-up — after rotating an org API key in Console, our Go SDK in the sampleapp kept serving 401s. We set the new REDWOOD_API_KEY in the CI job but the running container kept using the old key until I restarted it.

maya: repro steps?

tom: Repro: rotate key in Console -> CI exports REDWOOD_API_KEY=new -> deploy -> app logs 401. We confirmed the env var inside the container is the new value, but the SDK is still using a cached token file (~/.redwood/credentials). Log snippet: 
```bash
2026-03-15T14:02:01Z ERROR auth: token invalid (401)
2026-03-15T14:02:02Z WARN auth: falling back to cached credential file at /home/app/.redwood/credentials
```

kevin: This is expected given the cache behavior we added to support offline dev (cached credentials with no TTL). But we never added a reload-on-env-change path. JS SDK always prefers env when present, Go currently checks file first then env.

leo: Two low-effort mitigations: (1) prefer env over file if REDWOOD_API_KEY exists, (2) add a SIGHUP handler to reload credentials from disk/env for long-lived processes. Both would avoid container restarts.

maya: Also note parity gap: python and js keep env precedence, go and rust don't. We should standardize behavior across SDKs (env wins, then file, then metadata service).

kevin: Implementation note: changing precedence is safe but we should add a small integration test. Alternative for CI teams: set a sentinel env var REDWOOD_CRED_VERSION and bump it after rotation; SDK will watch the sentinel and force reload when it changes. No restart required.

tom: I like the sentinel idea (low churn), but long-running processes still benefit from SIGHUP. I'll open an issue with repro instructions and link the sampleapp.

leo: sgtm. For production Dedicated customers we might also want an explicit SDK API: client.RefreshCredentials(ctx) so orchestrators can call it on rotation.

deploy-bot: CI job #3421 failed :x: — auth 401, redeploy blocked.

maya: I'll add a small test in the sdk-integration suite to assert env precedence and add the sentinel test. Tagging @eng-runtime for awareness about extra filewatch or signal handlers.

tom: Thanks. Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/987 — contains repro steps, logs, and a tiny sampleapp change that demonstrates the cached-file fallback.

kevin: I'll pick up the Go fix (env precedence + optional SIGHUP). Will include a feature flag so we can opt-in while we land tests.

tom: Awesome — please post PR link here when ready and ping QA for integration test runs.
